articles.title: FSU running back signs with NFC North team
articles.summary: Roydell Williams was not selected during the 2026 NFL Draft but he will get a shot after signing with the Detroit Lions as the preseason rolls on.
articles.body:
Roydell Williams will have the opportunity to play for an NFL team.

The former FSU running back was not selected during the 2026 NFL Draft but has signed with the Detroit Lions as the preseason nears its conclusion. The team posted the info to their X page, although details of the contract were not disclosed.

Williams spent two seasons with the Seminoles, joining the team as a transfer from the Alabama Crimson Tide in 2024. At FSU, he played in 10 games and rushed for 99 yards and two touchdowns, but was injured for much of his time in Tallahassee. With the Crimson Tide, he totaled 1,165 rushing yards and scored 11 touchdowns.

He reunites with Alabama teammate Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit, who is their feature back. Detroit has been looking for depth at the running back position, and it's possible Williams shores it up.

The Detroit Lions went 9-8 last season under head coach Dan Campbell, missing the playoffs last season in the suddenly hyper-competitive NFC North. The Lions have the sixth-easiest strength of schedule in the league this season, so whether they can bounce back and return to the playoffs remains to be seen.

articles.title: Texans predicted to replace David Montgomery in 2027 ESPN mock draft with 24-TD Ole Miss RB
articles.summary: This would be a bold decision from the Texans after just trading for Montgomery.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans ' defense is one of, if not the best, units in the NFL. Even with a mediocre offense, this defense should carry the Texans to the playoffs.

But, that doesn't mean they shouldn't be looking to upgrade the offense. The tight end and wide receiver rooms aren't terrible, but they're in flux. The offensive line is shaky and C.J. Stroud might not be the franchise guy after bad end 2026.

The running back room is very strong, but ESPN's Jordan Reid is predicting they're going to replace David Montgomery or Woody Marks in the 2027 NFL Draft by taking 24-touchdown Ole Miss RB Kewan Lacy.

Texans predicted to replace their starting RBs with Kewan Lacy

"20. Houston Texans . Kewan Lacy, RB, Ole Miss," Reid predicts. "The Texans have a deep roster, but they could use some reinforcements at running back."

Even though the Texans just traded for Montgomery this offseason, Reid is predicting they prepare to move on from the veteran RB, as he's turning 30 years old next season.

Marks has shown flashes, but Reid is still predicting the Texans land Lacy, the best running back in next year's draft class, in the first round of this ESPN mock draft.

Lacy ran the ball 306 times for 1,567 yards and 24 touchdowns for the Ole Miss Rebels last year. That's incredibly impressive, and something that any RB-needy team would love to add to their roster next year.

But first-round running backs cost a lot, and might not be worth it. Though in this mock draft scenario, using the 20th pick on Lacy wouldn't be a terrible overpay considering his talents.

If he has another huge season in 2026, then Lacy might not even make it down the board this far. The upside with Lacy is incredible, and the Texans could use a superstar on offense outside of Nico Collins .

Montgomery and Marks are good running backs, but landing someone as good as Lacy, with the hope that he turns into one of the best RBs in the NFL, is intriguing enough to spend a first-round pick on him.

articles.title: Stock Up: Which Cowboys are trending heading into preseason finale?
articles.summary: The depth at receiver and running back, plus Ajani Cornelius at right guard, have all raised their stock for the Cowboys' offense.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys defeated the Arizona Cardinals, 34-13 ; their second convincing preseason victory. In both contests, the defense showed up and played extremely well, but this time the offense followed suit. Joe Milton getting the start and going off is the biggest reason. He threw for 179 yards and two touchdowns plus ran in another score.

Beyond his well documented and heavily discussed success, there are still other areas which were bolded question marks coming into the exhibition schedule. There was the battle between the receivers below the top three options, as well as the running back group beyond Javonte Williams .

With one preseason game left to go that will almost certainly see the majority of players expected to see regular-season action on the sidelines, here's whose stock is highest.

Ajani Cornelius moved from tackle over to guard and played almost 100 preseason snaps. His PFF overall grade is 87.3, and he hasn't allowed the quarterback to be touched, giving up only two pressures in 50 pass-blocking reps. This is incredibly important for a Cowboys team badly needing offensive line depth after losing multiple solid backups in free agency. The offensive line hasn't been a strong suit, with most believing T.J. Bass is the only reserve who could start if any of the starting five were injured. If Cornelius can be a backup offensive guard with a ton of college right tackle experience, it could reset the depth on the unit.

Another solid performance this Friday against the Saints , in what should be an extended look, could earn him a spot on the 53-man roster.

The running back room has a top-end starter in Williams, and the depth begins with the guy nobody seems to want, Malik Davis . He isn't flashy, but he doesn't have major holes in his game. He gets what's blocked for him on run plays, he can bring in a pass, his blocking is as good as Williams, and he plays special teams at a high level.

In the latest preseason game, he caught a touchdown pass, blocked in pass protection to set up a big play, and rushed for nearly 6 yards per attempt. Dallas has their main backup, and the change-of-pace option finally showed up in Arizona.

Jaydon Blue is who fans want as the backup, as he has an explosive element the Cowboys are currently missing from their rushing attack. Blue ran the ball 15 times for 75 yards and looked like an NFL rusher. He ran between the tackles and fell forward as he was being tackled. The guys likely to make the practice squad, Israel Abanikanda and Phil Mafah , both also had good moments against the Cardinals .

Mafah took his only carry for a 15-yard touchdown without great blocking to lead him, and Abanikanda had eight rushes for 49 yards. The whole room showed up well in the second preseason game, and Friday's contest could be a deciding factor in not just the 53-man roster, but also the practice squad.

Camden Brown began the year as possibly the last receiver on the depth chart. If he were only judged on this camp, Jonathan Mingo would probably be a lock for the roster. The two are battling it out for the fifth receiver spot, and the fact that it's them atop the heap is a shock to most.

Marquez Valdes-Scantling is a known vet who some thought could take Mingo's spot. Tyler Johnson and Denzel Mims are other veterans with production in NFL games, and Anthony Smith was a 2026 draft pick.

Brown shouldn't compete for the fifth receiving position, but he is because he has had an incredible camp. He has led the team in receiving yards both games, and his stat line of seven targets, five catches, 139 yards, and two touchdowns is impressive.

Mingo finally showing what made him a second-round pick, along with excellent special-teams play could have the edge. The teams play is a key to being the fifth receiver option, and a 53-yard, deep-ball touchdown reception have Mingo right in the mix. He is the second-highest-graded receiver in the preseason for Pro Football Focus with a grade of 90.5. The receiving battle for the fifth spot could force the Cowboys into keeping six receivers.

articles.title: SEC to issue harsh punishments for teams that add former pro athletes
articles.summary: The SEC is finalizing some harsh penalties for teams that violate its new professional players ban in the conference.
articles.body:
The SEC has settled on some harsh punishments for any member schools that sign a former professional player to its roster going forward, according to multiple reports on Wednesday, Aug. 26.

The conference unanimously passed ruling to ban former professional players from returning to college on Aug. 25, following a vote. Teams in violation of the SEC's new rules against former professional athletes returning to college will receive the following penalties:

50% of season suspension for head coaches

50% of that sport's annual operating budget

SEC voting privileges revoked on some matters

It's a gloves-off approach for the SEC, which is taking a hard stance against players entering the professional ranks before attempting to change their minds and return to college. The ruling comes amid multiple former NFL signees attempting returns to college football after gaining an extra season of eligibility, thanks to a temporary restraining order ruling in Louisiana state court this offseason.

"College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference ," the SEC's statement read on Aug. 25. "Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition.

"Allowing that to occur will blur the line between college and professional sports, create significant competitive equity concerns, and reduce opportunities for high school and current college athletes."

The Big Ten was the first Power Four conference to agree on rules against the situation, which has gained attention after LSU has added former Ole Miss standouts Dae'Quan Wright and Xzavian Harris, who both signed NFL contracts as undrafted free agents. The two players played under head coach Lane Kiffin for the Rebels, and gained extra seasons due to the court decision, which had a basis due to the NCAA's new 5-for-5 eligibility ruling.

It's unclear how the ruling impacts Wright and Harris' eligibility moving forward.

Kiffin told Pat McAfee on Aug. 25 that he doesn't agree with professional players returning to the college ranks, but that Wright and Harris' situation was different based on 5-for-5.

"There's a lot of parts of this I don't like," Kiffin said. "I don't think professionals should come back to college sports and college football. But in this instance, these are not players who have gone on to play seasons professionally or randomly filed an injunction. This is part of a specific class that was ruled wrong by the NCAA that was supposed to be 5-for-5."

SEC punishments for signing former professional player

The SEC's new punishments bar any team from signing former professional players from any level, whether it's the NBA's G-League, the NFL or the WNBA, for example.

articles.title: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst says team is 'prepared' for possible Josh Jacobs suspension
articles.summary: Josh Jacobs has yet to face punishment from the NFL after a May arrest.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was arrested in May and booked on five charges following an alleged domestic-violence situation. At the time, the NFL said it was aware of the situation, but has yet to issue any sort of punishment against the running back.

But the Packers know a suspension is a possibility, and are "prepared" for that scenario, team general manager Brian Gutekunst told reporters Wednesday.

When asked about Jacobs' situation, Gutekunst took it as an opportunity to say the team feels good about its depth at running back.

With just two weeks to go until the start of the 2026 NFL regular season, the league needs to act quickly if Jacobs is going to miss time early in the regular season. It's unclear whether that will happen.

The NFL typically likes to let the legal process play out before issuing suspensions to players. That's the track the league took with New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara following a 2022 arrest. With Kamara's legal situation still ongoing at the start of the 2022 NFL season, the league waited to issue discipline to the running back. Kamara was allowed to play and took part in 15 games before the league issued a three-game suspension to Kamara ahead of the 2023 NFL season.

But the league might feel compelled to act early in this instance. During an August radio appearance in Milwaukee, ESPN's Adam Schefter said the league could look to be proactive in Jacobs' case. While Schefter hedged with his reporting, he ultimately said he would "not be surprised if there is discipline by the time the season starts."

When on the field, Jacobs has proven to be an excellent, durable runner. In two seasons with the Packers, he's rushed for 2,258 yards and 28 touchdowns.

If Jacobs is suspended in 2026, his workload would fall to some combination of Chris Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd . Since being drafted in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft, Lloyd has played in just one game due to injuries.

Brooks, meanwhile, has spent the last two years in Green Bay . He's received 63 rushing attempts over that period, gaining 289 yards and scoring one touchdown.

articles.title: Tua to Start Falcons' Preseason Finale, Stefanski Updates Timeline to Name QB1 amid Penix Jr. Return
articles.summary: While most NFL teams typically rest their key players in the final preseason game, Atlanta Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski won't have that luxury in Friday's finale against the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body:
While most NFL teams typically rest their key players in the final preseason game, Atlanta Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski won't have that luxury in Friday's finale against the Miami Dolphins.

Stefanski told reporters on Wednesday that veteran quarterback Tua Tagovailoa will be the starter for Friday's game, and fellow signal-callers Cooper Rush and Jack Strand will also see action. Despite third-year quarterback Michael Penix Jr. being cleared to practice fully earlier this week, Stefanski added he feels it's "too early" to put him in a game.

When asked when he will name the Falcons' starter for the 2026 campaign, Stefanski said he's not sure and added, "I just know it's not today."

Buzz: Bain (Shoulder) Will Play Week 1 🙌

Penix underwent left ACL surgery in November and had only participated in individual drills and 7-on-7 periods before returning to full participation this week. The 26-year-old told reporters that even though he feels healthy enough to start in Week 1 against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sept. 13, he's content with sitting out the preseason finale.

"I'm not playing this week, because I only had three practices under my belt doing 11 on 11," he said, adding , "I just got cleared. Let me get my feet wet a little bit."

Tagovailoa played briefly in Atlanta's preseason opener against the Denver Broncos, completing three of his five passes for 22 yards in a 27-7 loss. He sat out Saturday's 34-6 loss to the Indianapolis Colts. Strand, who joined the Falcons as an undrafted free agent, impressed with 212 yards and a touchdown on 12-of-17 passing and a rushing score in the loss. Rush also looked solid, as the longtime backup went 10-of-11 for 86 yards.

While Tagovailoa could have the edge over Penix in Atlanta's quarterback competition by playing on Friday, it sounds like Stefanski is in no rush to make a decision, and Penix will still have time to prove himself before the starter is determined.

articles.title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson Will Do 'Whatever It Takes to Win' After Injury Limited Carries in 2025
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson amassed a career-low 67 carries last season as he dealt with numerous injuries and ultimately missed four games.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson amassed a career-low 67 carries last season as he dealt with numerous injuries and ultimately missed four games.

However, Jackson made it clear during a conversation with ESPN's Jamison Hensley during a Wednesday press conference with reporters that he will do "whatever it takes to win."

"I believe you know, I know, a lot of people know, I was hurt last year too. I really couldn't do anything I wanted to, so it really wouldn't put my team in a good position if I was just running hurt, losing yards, things like that was happening. But whatever it takes to win, that's what I'm all about. And I've always been about that too."

Hensley then asked Jackson if his thought his running attempts in 2026 would be more in line with seasons prior to 2025.

"Whatever it takes to win," Jackson replied.

Jackson has been a prolific runner. From 2019 (his first full year as the Ravens' starting quarterback) through 2024, Jackson rushed for 5,478 yards (913 yards per season) and 28 touchdowns on an average of 144.5 attempts per season (6.3 YPC).

However, those rushing attempt numbers had been in a bit of a decline over time even before 2025, as Adam Levitan of Establish the Run pointed out.

In 2025, as Jackson dealt with numerous ailments, he ran for 349 yards and a pair of scores (5.2 yards per carry). He ran 5.2 times per game after doing so just under 10 times per game (9.97) from 2019-2024.

Obviously, a healthy Jackson who can perform as a dual threat would be a massive win for the Ravens, who have gone 76-31 in his starts over eight seasons.

This is also a crucially important season for the Ravens, who just missed the playoffs after an 8-9 campaign and are looking to get new head coach Jesse Minter's era off to a good start.

Based on Jackson's remarks, he'll be running more in 2026. The question is whether he goes back to his old habit of running for about 10 times per game, or close to it. Regardless, a healthy Jackson running more often is a big win for the Ravens as they hope for a bounce-back season.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker III's Ankle Injury Caused by Shoe Issue, Chiefs' Andy Reid Says
articles.summary: New Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III has missed the last two days of action in training camp, and Andy Reid explained his absence on Wednesday.
articles.body:
New Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III has missed the last two days of action in training camp, and Andy Reid explained his absence on Wednesday.

The Chiefs' head coach told reporters that Walker has been dealing with ankle swelling because of a shoe issue.

The good news for the Chiefs is that Walker was not wearing a boot or a brace on his foot, though he was still held out of practice on Wednesday.

Walker, a second-round pick in 2022, is entering his first season with the Chiefs after spending the first four years of his career with the Seattle Seahawks. He's coming off a season in which he recorded 1,027 rushing yards and five touchdowns along with 282 receiving yards.

He rushed for 135 yards in the Super Bowl against the New England Patriots, enough for him to earn Super Bowl MVP.

Kansas City signed Walker to a three-year, $43.05 million contract this offseason as it looks to ramp up the backfield and get back to the playoffs after missing last season.

The rushing attack doesn't extend much further behind Walker. His backup is Emari Demercado, who had just 312 rushing yards for the Arizona Cardinals last year. Behind Demercado is rookie running back Emmett Johnson, a fifth-round pick out of Nebraska.

While Walker's injury doesn't appear to be too serious, it adds to a list of ailments the Chiefs are dealing with in training camp.

Safety Chamarri Conner (knee), defensive end Ashton Gillotte (foot), safety Alohi Gilman (back), offensive lineman C.J. Hanson (undisclosed), wide receiver Jimmy Holiday (quad), quarterback Chris Oladokun (concussion), left tackle Josh Simmons (back) and defensive end Tyreke Smith (hamstring) all did not practice on Tuesday.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors Clarify Rules on Players' Future Draft Status After Returning to CFB
articles.summary: With a handful of NFL players attempting to return to college football, the league has clarified how returning to the collegiate level will impact those players' draft statuses.
articles.body:
With a handful of NFL players attempting to return to college football, the league has clarified how returning to the collegiate level will impact those players' draft statuses.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter, any player who has signed an NFL contract and then is cut is a free agent. He can then join another NFL team, the CFL or return to college, but will be considered a free agent and won't be a part of a future draft.

Schefter also noted that a player who returns to college football this year will not be able to sign with an NFL team this season.

The ruling from the NFL comes in the aftermath of a Louisiana court passing a temporary restraining order that granted several players who have signed with NFL teams the opportunity to return to college football.

One of the most notable names in that case is former Cleveland Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright, who committed to Lane Kiffin and LSU on Tuesday after clearing waivers following his release from the Browns. If he ends up playing for the Tigers, he'll be the first player to go from an NFL roster back to college.

Max Olson of ESPN reported Thursday that Wright, former SMU running back TJ Harden, former BYU offensive lineman Weylin Lapuaho, former Ole Miss defensive lineman Zxavian Harris, former James Madison linebacker Trent Hendrick, former Appalachian State cornerback Ethan Johnson and former New Mexico kicker Luke Drzewiecki are entering the portal.

The SEC and Big Ten on Tuesday passed rule changes that prohibit schools in their league from adding players who have previously declared for the NFL, NBA or WNBA drafts and did not withdraw within the allowed timeframe.

The Big 12 and Notre Dame are reported to be heading in that direction as well, while the ACC will have discussions later this week.

What that rule change means for Wright and other players who have entered the portal with the intention of returning to college remains to be seen, but all parties are navigating uncharted waters.

"I feel like I took a freakin' gummy," the Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters when asked about NFL players returning to college.

While there is still plenty of figuring out to do among NFL and college athletics leaders, the league's clarification on Wednesday at least offers more of an answer about how players' draft statuses will be impacted if they go back to college.

articles.title: Titans' $28 Ticket Price In Honor of Chris Johnson to Benefit ALS Research Revealed
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans are honoring former running back Chris Johnson, who revealed in June he was diagnosed with ALS, with a ticket promotion that will generate money for research into the disease.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans are honoring former running back Chris Johnson, who revealed in June he was diagnosed with ALS, with a ticket promotion that will generate money for research into the disease.

Tennessee announced Wednesday that 2,000 tickets for its Sept. 13 opener against the New York Jets will be available for $28 each. Johnson wore No. 28 when he played for the Titans.

Five dollars from each ticket sale will be donated to the Vanderbilt ALS Research Center.

Johnson publicly announced his diagnosis in June during an appearance on Good Morning America .

"There's no history of ALS in my family," he told Michael Strahan. "My doctors believe my case is what's called sporadic ALS, which is actually how the vast majority of ALS cases happen. That's one of the reasons this disease can be so shocking. It can happen to someone who never expected it."

Shortly after the interview aired, Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk released a statement:

"We will support Chris every step of the way throughout his journey," the statement said, in part. "We are holding him and his family close, and join our fans around the world in expressing our love for Chris."

The Titans selected Johnson with a first-round pick in the 2008 NFL draft. He played his first six seasons for the team and ran for more than 1,000 yards in each of them.

He was a three-time Pro Bowler during that span and even led the league with 2,006 rushing yards during the 2009 campaign.

Johnson then played for the Jets and the Arizona Cardinals during his final four seasons.

articles.title: As mental health concerns spike, NFL launches network to provide offsite clinicians to players and their families
articles.summary: The network launch comes in the wake of a spring announcement by the league to increase mental health resources in three tiers following the deaths by suicid...
articles.body:
The NFL is expanding the mental health resources available to players and their families.

Beginning Sept. 1, NFL players and any family members on their insurance plan will gain access to a network of vetted clinicians in every NFL city. Players can use these resources, in addition to in-house clinicians, without visit limits or coinsurance requirements, NFL vice president of wellness and clinical services Dr. Nyaka NiiLampti told Yahoo Sports.

The network launch comes in the wake of a spring announcement by the league to increase mental health resources in three tiers following the deaths by suicide of Cowboys defensive end Marshawn Kneeland and Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Rondale Moore last November and February, respectively.

The league announced in March that it was increasing its in-house clinical presence to require teams to staff full-time mental health clinicians, up from the previous requirement that teams staff clinicians at least eight to 12 hours a week as mandated by the NFL-NFLPA collective bargaining agreement. The NFL also has sought to increase efforts to support the mental health of players battling injuries, as Moore had in the years prior to his death. And the NFL and NFLPA partnered with Cigna Healthcare to create this network.

"Historically the sense was that players don't use mental health resources," NiiLampti told Yahoo Sports by phone on Tuesday. "Sports is a microcosm of society. So in the last few years we've seen everybody increase their use of mental health resources and this population is no different. And so we've probably had more difficulties trying to find a provider than we have had people willing to use the resource.

"I like to say we're way past awareness. We're really into action."

The behavioral network aims to smooth access to clinical support for current and eligible former players, as well as all family members who are on their insurance plans.

NFL and NFLPA staff worked to identify providers with experience navigating the mental health challenges that most stress professional athletes.

The league aims to have at least three to five tabbed clinicians in NFL cities, as well as markets with strong former player presences, NiiLampti said.

"Anybody who has had to navigate the mental health system knows how cumbersome that can be," NiiLampti said. "I'm a psychologist and it's difficult to navigate. So … the goal is to remove as many barriers as possible to members of the community who are interested in seeking support."

Players will still have access to on-site clinicians who can either support them directly or refer them to these offsite providers. The providers are available for in-person as well as virtual visits. NiiLampti estimated that the pre-identification of these providers could eliminate four to five hours of research for team clinicians aiming to provide players with the best possible referrals.

She expects some players will still avail themselves of in-house clinicians.

"What we're seeing is more and more players are comfortable with using the in-house clinical," NiiLampti said. "It limits them having to travel."

But the league is realistic about some employees' concerns visiting a clinical provider who works for their employer and is hosted on site. While players can connect with network providers through in-house clinicians, they can also connect with off-site clinicians independent of in-house resources.

"We will always be in a position where players might not trust the resources that are in the building," NiiLampti said. "And so one of the things that we really made sure will happen on this one as well is that players can directly access this referral network so they don't have to go through somebody at the club to find a provider.

"They can actually access it on their own."

The NFLPA had previously given players a clinical directory, but this collectively bargained network will create a support system for scheduling visits that are covered at 100%. The league and union have worked to encourage current and former players to be more proactive about their physical and mental health , a move that experts say is players' best option when facing concerns about degenerative brain conditions such as the football-associated neurological degeneration called CTE.

Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn echoed that message after Moore's death in February.

"I'm hopeful that we get to a point that we're not talking about mental health just when a tragedy hits, but that we are talking about it on a regular basis," Quinn said. "Then we know we're making real strides."

Players will receive mail and email blasts to alert them of the behavioral network. Clubs are also required to complete mental health education sessions. Those sessions predated the deaths of Kneeland and Moore. But the league recognizes how player suicides can change the tenor of these trainings.

"I'd say that the conversations probably hit a little bit differently this year," NiiLampti said. "The more that we can encourage folks to, again, think about where they are, check in on each other and use the resources, I think that's the goal."

articles.title: Cam Skattebo 'Started a Fight' with Giants Teammates, NFL Insider Reveals 'His Act is Getting Old'
articles.summary: Some of Cam Skattebo's New York Giants teammates reportedly did not appreciate the running back's actions during Wednesday's practice.
articles.body:
Some of Cam Skattebo's New York Giants teammates reportedly did not appreciate the running back's actions during Wednesday's practice.

Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reported Skattebo "started a fight" when he "came dangerously close to taking out" the legs of multiple defensive backs when he slid down following a reception. Leonard listed Jevon Holland and Greg Newsome among those who were upset.

He also suggested the running back's "act is getting old to his defensive teammates" after he also ran over linebacker Zaire Barnes during a previous practice when the defense was not allowed to hit.

Even head coach John Harbaugh told reporters, "He got a 15-yard penalty at the end of practice," when asked about Skattebo's infectious energy. "Did you see that? Yeah it's infectious. It can be infectious the other way, an infectious disease type of thing. We want it to be in a positive way."

Skattebo is known for his physical running style and embrace of contact. He is also quite energetic when on the field.

The Giants know this and even appeared to embrace it last season when they asked some of his teammates to do their best impressions of the running back:

Still, embracing that contact with your own team's defensive players or coming close to making dangerous plays, especially when they are not allowed to hit during practice sessions, isn't going to sit well with his teammates.

It became such an issue Wednesday that his head coach compared his energy to an "infectious disease," which is sure to turn heads.

Fortunately for the Giants, the season is just weeks away. They start the 2026 campaign on Sept. 13 against the rival Dallas Cowboys, which means Skattebo will have the opportunity to run over defenders on another team instead of his own.

His overall effectiveness will be a major storyline, as he was limited to just eight games during his rookie season in 2025 because of a fractured tibia and dislocated ankle. If he returns to the form he demonstrated before his setback, the Giants could have a dangerous offense with wide receiver Malik Nabers on the outside.

Skattebo tallied 410 rushing yards, 207 receiving yards and seven total touchdowns in eight games last season. He was also listed as the starting running back on the team's unofficial depth chart ahead of the preseason finale against the New York Jets, per ESPN's Jordan Raanan .

That seems to be a positive indication the Giants believe he is back and ready to go from the injury, although he was reportedly not the most popular figure during Wednesday's practice.

articles.title: NFL and Players Association Announce Behavioral Health Network for Mental Health Assistance
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — The NFL and NFL Players Association on Wednesday announced a Behavioral Health Network will launch on Sept. 1 and will be designed to provide simplified and confidential access to mental health assistance.
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — The NFL and NFL Players Association on Wednesday announced a Behavioral Health Network will launch on Sept. 1 and will be designed to provide simplified and confidential access to mental health assistance.

The new network is an enhancement to the NFL Player Insurance Plan that expands access to confidential outpatient behavioral health support for current and former players and their eligible dependents.

The national network of behavioral health providers will be administered by Cigna Healthcare. It is designed to support the unique needs of current and former players and their families.

Report: NFL to Continue Taunting Crackdown

The national network will include every NFL market. Players will have access to personalized support that includes assistance with provider searches, appointment availability and benefit questions.

There will be no charge or coinsurance fee to the players for the outpatient services provided by the network. There is no limit to the number of visits.

"The goal of the Behavioral Health Network is to make it easier for players and their families to access clinical support," said Dr. Nyaka NiiLampti, NFL vice president of wellness and clinical services, in a statement.

"Our priority is to remove barriers to care and ensure that members of the NFL community can quickly identify and connect with trusted mental health providers. By simplifying and streamlining the process to find high-quality mental health services, we hope this enhancement will improve delivery of care and support better wellness related outcomes."

NFLPA director of player wellness Dr. Amber Cargill said "mental and emotional well-being" are priorities as well as protecting the physical health of players.

"Every player's needs are different," Cargill said. "The Behavioral Health Network marks an important step in expanding access to trusted care for players and their families while continuing to build a culture where seeking support is encouraged."

articles.title: NFL's New Rules for Fines, Suspensions Revealed with Emphasized Punishment for Repeat Offenders
articles.summary: The NFL is hoping to improve player health and safety with the implementation of a new disciplinary system.
articles.body:
The NFL is hoping to improve player health and safety with the implementation of a new disciplinary system.

The NFL and NFLPA announced Wednesday that players will receive an automatic suspension if they commit three offenses in categories including hip-drop tackle, horse collar tackle, launching, hit on a defenseless player and blindside block.

If a player commits only one offense, they will receive 50 percent of their fine back at the end of the season.

Report: NFL to Continue Taunting Crackdown

The new system was developed in collaboration with the NFL Players Association. NFLPA president Troy Vincent told Mark Maske of Front Office Sports that the system is in place for one year only.

"Just to see if it works," Vincent said .

Each player will enter the 2026 season with a clean slate. Players who commit one violation will have 50 percent of their fine returned to them at the end of the year. A single offense in certain eligible categories would allow players to receive the entire amount of their fine back once the season ends.

It was also noted that the NFL will meet with players who are approaching the suspension threshold, and their head coaches are required to attend those meetings. Teams with "excessive" rule violations will be subjected to increased financial penalties. Former NFL head coach Ron Rivera, who also played in the league for nine seasons, will be added to the pool of former players who oversee disciplinary appeal hearings.

Player safety has become a greater point of emphasis for the league, and the new on-field accountability system could lead to continued improvements in that area.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. Hyped by John Harbaugh Ahead of Decision on Giants' Roster Cuts
articles.summary: As Odell Beckham Jr. eyes a spot on the New York Giants ahead of roster cuts at the end of the week, he received high praise from head coach John Harbaugh.
articles.body:
As Odell Beckham Jr. eyes a spot on the New York Giants ahead of roster cuts at the end of the week, he received high praise from head coach John Harbaugh.

"Odell's had a good camp," Harbaugh told reporters on Wednesday. "His best week of camp has come this week."

After going unsigned during the 2025 campaign, Beckham joined the Giants in June, setting up a reunion with the team where he started his career.

"Most people don't get a chance to double back," the veteran receiver told reporters earlier this month. "This is a place that made me into a man, made me into who I am. I have so much love for this organization, this city. I got 'New York' tatted on my back, you know what I mean? I'm from New Orleans. All I ever wanted to do was win a championship for the New York Giants."

But his return to New York this summer didn't guarantee that he'd be on the roster once the season began. He's still fighting for a spot in the final weeks of training camp.

ESPN's Jordan Raanan reported on Aug. 10 that Beckham is competing with Braxton Berrios and Dalen Cambre for the final spot on the roster.

The competition for the final roster spot might have changed this week, though, as wide receiver Calvin Austin III suffered a season-ending torn ACL on Tuesday. That's unfortunate news for the Giants' depth, but it could make it a bit easier for Beckham to secure a spot on the roster.

Beckham has spent most of the offseason as a reserve option but has occasionally worked with New York's first-team offense. He's also shown some vintage moments throughout camp.

Through two preseason games, Beckham has recorded four receptions for 23 yards.

The 33-year-old Beckham was an All-Pro caliber receiver during his first tenure with the Giants, but injuries derailed his career a bit, and he hasn't recorded a 1,000-plus receiving yard season since 2019. He last played for the Miami Dolphins in 2024, where he recorded just nine receptions for 55 yards.

He's looking to revitalize his career in New York, but he'll have to finish out the week strong to ensure he makes the 53-man roster.

articles.title: Pro Bowl Game Eliminated by NFL, Players Will Still Be Chosen for Honors with No Alternates
articles.summary: The NFL is eliminating the Pro Bowl Game following a presentation from league executives to team owners, according to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic.
articles.body:
The NFL is eliminating the Pro Bowl Game following a presentation from league executives to team owners, according to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic.

Per Jones, the Pro Bowl is set to become an individual performance award with 88 players receiving the honor for each season. There will be no more Pro Bowl alternates.

Instead of a game, Pro Bowlers will be invited to Los Angeles for an in-person celebration in February of each year.

The Pro Bowl format has changed on several occasions in order to generate more fan interest and limit the amount of players opting out, moving from a clash between AFC and NFC stars to two honorary team captains selecting their rosters from 2014-16 before switching back.

Pro Bowl festivities have also been held in different locations including Hawaii, Orlando and San Francisco.

Starting in 2023, the Pro Bowl changed to a flag-football contest while also implementing days of skills challenges that factored into the event.

The 2026 Pro Bowl Games averaged just 1.9 million viewers, representing an all-time low mark for the event (via Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk).

NFL executive vice president of club business, international and league events Peter O'Reilly discussed the removal of a game for the Pro Bowl.

"All-star games, I think, for all leagues have been fraught for a long time, and they haven't necessarily represented the very best premium of that sport for those players," O'Reilly told Jones. "I think all leagues have struggled with that. We made the switch four years ago from the 'tackle' Pro Bowl to the flag game, and that was more strategic for us. In many ways, we saw a decrease in the replacement players.

"But ultimately, the Pro Bowl, at its core, is about honoring the best of the best in that season, on the field, in real games. And the shift here is about shifting the focus from the game — which is ultimately where people's attention goes, especially the replacement players tied to it — to the honor."

Despite the change, fans, players and coaches will still vote on Pro Bowl selections moving forward.

articles.title: HBO 'Hard Knocks' NFL Offseason Edition Will Return in 2027, Details Revealed
articles.summary: It remains to be seen which division will be featured, but HBO's Hard Knocks will return next offseason.
articles.body:
It remains to be seen which division will be featured, but HBO's Hard Knocks will return next offseason.

NFL media announced Wednesday that its offseason edition will return in 2027 and chronicle four teams in a division as they build their rosters through the NFL draft process and free agency.

Episodes will air on HBO and be available on streaming on HBO Max.

"Our fans are increasingly interested in how NFL rosters are built, as well as the people who build them," NFL Films' senior executive Ross Ketover said. "With Hard Knocks moving to the offseason, we are excited to showcase the tireless work that happens across an entire division, from the moment a season ends to the minute training camp begins."

It won't be the first time an entire division has been featured on the show, as the AFC North was chronicled in 2024 before the NFC East was the focus in 2025. However, both of those editions took place during an actual season and focused more on games and the push for the playoffs.

The first such offseason edition aired in 2024 and just followed the New York Giants.

While it earned a Sports Emmy Award nomination, it also generated headlines because that was the same offseason star running back Saquon Barkley joined the Philadelphia Eagles after starting his career with the Giants.

Giants owner John Mara was seen in one of the episodes saying, "I might have a tough time sleeping if Saquon goes to Philadelphia."

Naturally, when Barkley did, in fact, go to Philadelphia, he ultimately won a Super Bowl with the Eagles.

Wednesday's Hard Knocks news comes as the series is following the Seattle Seahawks during training camp. Seattle won the Super Bowl last season and will look to defend the title, and HBO has provided a behind-the-scenes look at the team's preparation.

Hard Knocks will also return for training camp next year and feature the New England Patriots.

articles.title: New NFL fine schedule is going to a point system that could lead to suspensions but also refunds
articles.summary: The NFL and NFL Players Association agreed to a points-based fine system targeting hip drop tackles, horse collar tackles, and blindside blocks.
articles.body: The NFL and the NFL Players Association have agreed to a one-year experimental change to the fine schedule meant to perhaps curb player behavior and discipline that is most likely to result in injuries. And the changes include one seemingly odd new twist: Refunds. Club owners meeting in Atlanta on Wednesday were briefed and accepted the changes that will place greater emphasis on five player health and safety violations: NFL PLAYER REVEALS SUSPENSION FOR PERFORMANCE-ENHANCING DRUG HAPPENED BECAUSE HE WAS ADDRESSING INFERTILITY Like in the past, the league is prepared to take past behavior into account. That's why players who commit three offenses in any of the highlighted categories will be suspended for one game. But, here comes the newfangled approach: Players who commit just one violation will receive a 50 percent refund of their fine at the end of the season. The one violation limit applies to the five categories together. So a player fined for a blindside block cannot get a refund if he's also been fined once for a horse collar tackle. That amounts to two fines. NFL PLAYERS MAY COLLECTIVELY BARGAIN FOR GRASS FIELDS IN FUTURE NEGOTIATIONS BUT IT WOULD COME AT A COST The fine refunds apply to other categories of fouls as well and even to a larger degree. Players fined once in any other player safety category, such as roughing the passer, will get 100 percent of their fine money back at season's end if they don’t get fined again for that foul during the season. And, again, a second foul in another player safety category will mean the player gets none of his money back. This is expected to affect hundreds of players during the 2026 season as it has in previous seasons. This new system resembles the carrot and stick approach to fines. Players who avoid fines or stop after only one offense are rewarded with keeping or getting money back. Repeat offenders, however, get trouble. And so do their coaches and clubs. Repeat offenders lose all their fine money. And once they are within one point of the suspension threshold, they are subject to being called in to an official meeting with a league representative, along with members of his team's coaching staff. Clubs with "excessive" health and safety rules violations will also face increased financial penalties. This system also resembles the points system drivers all over the United States must abide by for their driving record. Everyone starts the 2026 season with a clean record. Each offense represents one point. Again, three points will mean a suspension. If a player has one point towards a suspension at the end of the season, he will drop to zero points entering the following season – assuming this experimental system remains or is not altered. If a driver, rather than a player, has two points at season's end, he’ll drop to one point. Players who are suspended this season will enter next season two points on their record, again assuming the system remains. "These changes focus on the techniques that create the greatest risk while ensuring player, coach, and club accountability. "Stop trying to create a BS Narrative" Eluemunor wrote on social media in response to a report from Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News that revealed Skattebo "started a fight" with reckless play that upset some of his defensive teammates who were not hitting.

"His act is getting old to his defensive teammates," Leonard added.

Eluemunor didn't like the "narrative" from the report, but enough happened for Giants head coach Jim Harbaugh to make quite a notable comment about the team's running back.

"He got a 15-yard penalty at the end of practice," Harbaugh told reporters when asked about Skattebo's infectious energy. "Did you see that? Yeah it's infectious. It can be infectious the other way, an infectious disease type of thing. We want it to be in a positive way."

It should be noted training camp scuffles and fights happen all the time, both at joint practices with other teams and between teammates.

By late August, teams have been dealing with heat and grueling practices for weeks and are surely ready for the regular-season games to begin. That can lead to some frustration, which can lead to those scuffles.

Still, Harbaugh's quote could serve as something of a wake-up call for Skattebo.

His actions were enough for the head coach to compare his energy to that of an "infectious disease" while also pushing for it to be used in a more positive way moving forward.

Skattebo's offensive teammates may have his back, as Eluemunor's comment suggests, but a head coach saying something like that is sure to catch the running back's attention.

If he internalizes it and uses his energy in a more positive way, perhaps he can lead the Giants to a successful season on the offensive side of the ball alongside young playmakers such as Malik Nabers and Jaxson Dart.

articles.title: Bijan Robinson Reveals Michael Penix Jr.'s Bold Claim amid Falcons QB's Injury Rehab
articles.summary: Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. apparently gained some speed while he was rehabbing a torn ACL this offseason.
articles.body:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. apparently gained some speed while he was rehabbing a torn ACL this offseason.

Star running back Bijan Robinson revealed a bold claim from Penix on Wednesday.

"He said this morning he'd beat me in a race," Robinson told reporters .

Penix has never been known for his speed or mobility, but if his claim of being faster than Robinson is true, he might have to start using his legs more often this season.

The first order of business for Penix is getting to 100 percent before the start of the season, and he made progress last week when he was cleared for 11-on-11. He'll now look to earn the starting job in Atlanta.

"The new part for Mike is just being in there in with a full offensive line, a full defensive line, but he's been in walkthrough huddles, he's been in 7-on-7, he's obviously gone through individuals," Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said this week. "So, this is a good—now that Mike is cleared—it's good that he can start that process of getting back to 11-on-11."

His apparent newfound speed should help in the battle against Tua Tagovailoa.

articles.title: Jeff Fisher Says Vince Young's Spelling Error Led Him to Not Respond to Apology Letter in Video
articles.summary: Former head coach Jeff Fisher said that he didn't respond to an apology letter from former quarterback Vince Young regarding the end of their shared tenure on the Tennessee Titans due to a spelling error.
articles.body:
Former head coach Jeff Fisher said that he didn't respond to an apology letter from former quarterback Vince Young regarding the end of their shared tenure on the Tennessee Titans due to a spelling error.

"You know, he spelled my name wrong," Fisher said in the documentary Untold: The Testimony of Vince Young (0:45 mark). "So I didn't know that it had come from him. I guess in retrospect it would have been nice to give him s--t about spelling my name wrong, you know?"

Young also explained what led to him sending the letter to Fisher.

"You know, I didn't want to leave anything open," Young said (0:21 mark). "No wounds open. So I was like, 'I hope you can forgive me for how I handled a lot of things with the Titans.' So that's why I sent him that letter."

Young and Fisher were both with the Titans from 2006-10, helping the team make two playoff appearances over that span.

During the 2010 season, they verbally clashed in the locker room following a Week 11 loss before Young wasn't permitted to attend a team meeting.

After Tennessee wrapped up a 6-10 finish that year, Fisher was fired before Young was released from the team.

articles.title: NFL ends Pro Bowl after decades of declining interest,  will turn all-star game into an award for 88 players
articles.summary: The NFL eliminated its AFC vs. NFC Pro Bowl game, ending skills competitions and flag football after ratings cratered to just 2 million viewers.
articles.body: The Pro Bowl is dead. The NFL finally laid its season-ending All-Star event to rest Wednesday. (This was a long time in coming because the Pro Bowl has been something of a corpse for years and the NFL has finally admitted it needed to be buried.) The NFL will no longer stage an AFC vs. NFC Pro Bowl game. Instead, the league will place greater emphasis on the moment a player is selected, the recognition that accompanies that distinction, and bringing the Pro Bowl class together to celebrate the achievement. "The Pro Bowl has always been about recognizing the players who distinguish themselves as the very best in the NFL," said Peter O’Reilly, NFL Executive Vice President, Club Business, International and League Events. "A Pro Bowl selection will return to its original purpose, honoring the best of the best. We want that distinction to carry even greater meaning for the players, their families, their clubs and our fans." Beginning with the 2026 season, 88 players will comprise the official Pro Bowl roster, with none of the replacement selections that in recent years diminished the honor. The roster will continue to be determined through an equal-weighted voting process among players, coaches and fans. By limiting the honor to the 88 players originally selected, the Pro Bowl will "return its focus squarely to recognizing the league’s most outstanding performers, reinforcing the significance of an achievement held in especially high regard by players themselves," the NFL said in a statement. This had to happen. The modern NFL Pro Bowl began in January of 1951, following the 1950 season, as an East-vs.-West all-star game. In 1971, it became the familiar AFC-vs.-NFC format. Its television high point came with the 2000 Pro Bowl, which drew 13.24 million viewers on ABC. After the league ended the tackle edition of the Pro Bowl in February 2022, it was replaced by the Pro Bowl Games in 2023. articles.title: NFL eliminating Pro Bowl event, prioritizing individual performance award without alternates
articles.summary: The Pro Bowl has taken on various forms over the years, and, in the process, the honor diminished with a flush of alternates.
articles.body:
The league is leaving the all-star competition in the past and prioritizing the Pro Bowl honor as an individual performance award without alternates.

League executives reportedly presented the future of the Pro Bowl to team owners on Wednesday. Without a standalone game or event to field, 88 players will receive Pro Bowl status every season.

"The Pro Bowl has always been about recognizing the players who distinguish themselves as the very best in the NFL," Peter O'Reilly, NFL executive vice president of club business and international and league events, said in a statement .

"A Pro Bowl selection will return to its original purpose, honoring the best of the best. We want that distinction to carry even greater meaning for the players, their families, their clubs and our fans."

In recent years, as the Pro Bowl experimented with different formats, including a flag football game that offered a bit more intensity but also an array of confusing rules, opt-outs increased. That left the league scrambling to fill spots with less qualified players who absorbed a Pro Bowl designation nonetheless. For instance, this past season, a pair of quarterbacks who started for a 5-12 Cleveland Browns team — Joe Flacco and Shedeur Sanders — were recognized as Pro Bowlers even though they were replacements for the game of flag.

They wound up helping the AFC build a big lead in a contest the NFC roared back to win 66-52 on a Tuesday night in San Francisco leading up to Super Bowl LX in nearby Santa Clara.

While flag and the other games the NFL has rolled out for the Pro Bowl have infused some fun into the two-week hiatus ahead of the big game, the surge in alternates stripped the Pro Bowl of its prestige and practically rendered any healthy discourse about snubs obsolete .

The NFL is now trying to renew the significance of being a Pro Bowler by solely emphasizing the accolade.

This season's Pro Bowlers will be invited to Los Angeles for an in-person celebration during the traditional Pro Bowl weekend.

An equal-weighted voting process among players, coaches and fans will continue to be used in determining the Pro Bowl roster. The class will be revealed in late December "through an enhanced announcement," according to a league release , which notes that Pro Bowlers' uniforms will be adorned with a "lasting and visible recognition" that'll serve as a symbol of their achievements.

During the 2025 campaign, the NFL tried holding its Pro Bowl in that season's Super Bowl market.

For decades, the Pro Bowl occurred the week after the Super Bowl. Aloha Stadium in Honolulu was home to the game for 30 straight years. Camping World Stadium in Orlando, Florida, eventually became a popular site for the event, and Las Vegas ' Allegiant Stadium was used to host it as well.

In the 2022 season, the Pro Bowl pivoted from its traditional tackle football game and turned to flag football and a skills competition.

Four seasons later, the Pro Bowl will only exist as an award.

"This direction came directly from our continued conversations with players and what they value most about the Pro Bowl," Troy Vincent , NFL executive vice president of football operations said in a statement.

"Being selected by your peers, coaches and fans as one of the very best at your position carries tremendous meaning. We heard clearly that the distinction matters, and our focus is on making the recognition that comes with it worthy of what these players accomplished on the field."

articles.title: NFL ends the Pro Bowl game, but players will still be honored as Pro Bowlers
articles.summary: The Pro Bowl is no more, the NFL announced Wednesday, ending an exhibition of the league’s top players that was held in some form almost every year since 1951.
articles.body: The Pro Bowl is no more, the NFL announced Wednesday, ending an exhibition of the league’s top players that was held in some form almost every year since 1951. The game wasn’t played in 2021 because of the COVID-19 pandemic, but that was the only pause in the postseason event. “It’s OK to be the first league to walk away from a competitive all-star game,” NFL executive vice president Peter O’Reilly said at the owners’ meeting in Atlanta. The league said 88 players will still be named as Pro Bowlers and honored in Los Angeles after this season. Several flag football events also will take place at that time. “The Pro Bowl has always been about recognizing the players who distinguish themselves as the very best in the NFL,” O’Reilly said in a statement. “A Pro Bowl selection will return to its original purpose, honoring the best of the best. We want that distinction to carry even greater meaning for the players, their families, their clubs and our fans.” O’Reilly said the decision was “a shift from the game to the honor.” Troy Vincent, the league’s executive vice president of football operations, said he heard from players that they “don’t want competitive play” after the playoffs. “You come off the championship games and the viewers see the physicality of the game and you try to replicate that,” Vincent said. “Frankly, it just doesn’t sit well. This isn’t a good representation.” The Pro Bowl has waned in popularity in recent years. Once a staple in Honolulu, the NFL has moved the event to various cities and even switched from tackle to flag football in 2023.

articles.title: Bills Face Unexpected Warning as Joe Brady Approaches First Season as HC
articles.summary: An NFL writer gave the Buffalo Bills an unexpected warning ahead of Joe Brady's first season as NFL head coach. The post Bills Face Unexpected Warning as Joe...
articles.body:
The Bills will kick off their season in less than three weeks when they take on the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. But is this a Super Bowl-or-bust season for Buffalo ?

While many people around the NFL think this is a Super Bowl-or-bust season for the Bills, Bleacher Report's Brad Gagnon doesn't view it that way.

Gagnon published an article listing every panic meter for all 32 NFL teams on Wednesday and rated the Bills' meter at 6/10.

" Josh Allen should have many good years ahead at 30, and the Bills are experimenting with a tweaked coaching staff. This remains in check for now but likely shoots up to nine if they fall short of the Super Bowl again in 2026," Gagnon wrote.

Joe Brady Shouldn't Be Pressured to Win the Super Bowl in His First Season

It makes sense for the Bills not to be in Super Bowl-or-bust mode this season, especially since they brought in a new head coach, Joe Brady, during the offseason. Just because Buffalo has one of the best rosters and a quarterback like Josh Allen, it doesn't mean winning a Super Bowl is a certainty this season.

The two most important things in the NFL are having a franchise quarterback and a good head coach. While the Bills have a great quarterback, nobody knows how Brady will do as head coach.

Brady has never been an NFL head coach, and putting so much pressure on him to win the Super Bowl in his first season isn't good for him.

The 36-year-old coach has a lot to learn in his first season, and rushing the process could do Brady more harm than good.

It would be nice to see the Bills make it to the Super Bowl, but realistically, winning the AFC East after losing the division to the New England Patriots last season, then winning a playoff game or two, would be a great first year for Brady.

If Brady can capitalize on his first-year success, he can carry that momentum into year two, when the Bills should be in "Super Bowl or bust" mode.

Allen Has Envisioned a Bills Super Bowl Parade

Although it may not be the Bills' season to win the Super Bowl, Allen certainly has visions of what winning a Super Bowl in Buffalo would look like.

"I can see the parade. I can feel it," Allen said last September, via CBS Sports Jordan Dajani. "Five degrees, brisk, rolling down, hearing the bus roll over all the salt and the ice. Thousands upon thousands of fans, filling up downtown Buffalo. I can see where we're going up on the steps at City Hall. I see it all. So, we gotta turn it into a reality."

If the Bills win a Super Bowl, no matter when it is, whether in the next few seasons or years from now, it will be one of the best celebrations and parties in sports history.

Buffalo has one of the best fan bases in all of sports, and its fans have been waiting a long time for a parade; it would be awesome for Allen to deliver the Super Bowl title.

articles.title: Seattle Seahawks: Reigning Super Bowl champions to be sold in record $9.6bn deal
articles.summary: NFL owners approve the $9.612bn record sale of the reigning Super Bowl champions Seattle Seahawks to a group led by billionaire Vinod Khosla.
articles.body:
NFL owners have approved the $9.612bn record sale of the reigning Super Bowl champions Seattle Seahawks to a group led by billionaire Vinod Khosla.

The deal, which required the support of at least 24 of 32 owners, is currently the second highest amount paid for a franchise in North American sports history.

The estate of Paul G. Allen, which inherited the NFL team after the death of the Microsoft co-founder in 2018, agreed to terms with the Khosla family on 11 July after a search for a new owner.

And now approved, the sale surpasses the $6.05bn the Washington Commanders fetched when they were sold in 2023, although the NBA's Los Angeles Lakers were subsequently sold for $10bn in 2025 and are currently in the process of changing ownership again for a reported $12.5bn.

"We are honoured to be entrusted as the next stewards of the Seattle Seahawks. How often do you get to buy a franchise that just won the Super Bowl?" said Khosla.

"We are incredibly lucky and humbled by this gift, I would say, from the Allen trust."

"We look forward to building on the winning legacy Paul Allen created and to earning the trust of the Seahawks organisation and fans everywhere."

Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, Khosla, who will have to relinquish a minority stake in the San Francisco 49ers as part of his agreement to buy the Seahawks, added: "The task ahead is actually pretty simple - keep the winning streak alive, get another Super Bowl.

"Our approach is generally going to be long-term focused, that's our inclination always. So, keep winning, take a long-term approach, and learn a lot. We don't know enough, and the other owners have been incredibly welcoming and willing to teach us, so we'll learn a lot.

"We'll learn from management and see what they are recommending."

Khosla, 71, was the co-founder of US technology company Sun Microsystems and the founder of the venture capital firm Khosla Ventures and has a net worth of $13.2bn, according to Forbes. , external

Former owner Allen saved the Seahawks from relocating to Southern California when he bought the team from Ken Behring in 1997.

His sister, Jody Allen, took control of the Seahawks and the NBA's Portland Trail Blazers as chair of both teams upon her brother's death with a directive to eventually sell both and donate the proceeds to charity.

In the 29 seasons in which Paul or Jody Allen were in charge, the Seahawks made the play-offs 17 times and won two of the four Super Bowls they contested.

articles.title: The NFL put its foot down on players returning to play at NCAA level
articles.summary: Amid the chaos surrounding college football eligibility, the NFL is providing clarity to clubs on its rules regarding the matter.
articles.body:
With the recent change in eligibility rules for the NCAA spurring a controversial series of lawsuits by members of the Class of 2022 recruiting cycle seeking the fifth year of eligibility they have been denied, some NFL players who exhausted four seasons of eligibility are now seeking to return to the collegiate level for an additional year if they are cut or waived by their current teams.

It's sparked an outcry among college sports fans, and college conferences such as the Big Ten, Big 12, and SEC have either already finalized or are in the process of finalizing policies to prevent such moves. And the NFL is also reaching out to clubs to make sure its rules on the matter are clear.

Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday that the league will not allow any player who goes back to play collegiate football in 2026 to sign another contract with an NFL team this year. Under league rules, any player signed to an NFL contract who is subsequently cut is a free agent. They are allowed to sign with another NFL team, sign with a CFL or UFL franchise, or return to college – but those players will be considered free agents and cannot be selected in a future draft.

The move comes after former Ole Miss tight end Dae'Quan Brown, who was signed by the Cleveland Browns this preseason, is seeking to return to the college level and follow former Ole Miss coach Lane Kiffin to LSU.

He, along with 15 other players, including former Ole Miss defensive lineman Xzavian Harris (signed with the Saints as an UDFA), Oregon State running back Anthony Hankerson (played during preseason with the Seahawks ), and SMU running back TJ Harden (played during preseason with the Seahawks ), was granted a temporary restraining order in court for an additional year.

The NFL's rules are obviously meant to discourage such moves, both by preventing the NFL from serving as a backup option later in the year with these players and by keeping the players from using another collegiate year as a springboard to becoming a higher draft pick next year. And it seems they are set to stand firm on their decision.

articles.title: NFL Eliminates Pro Bowl Game
articles.summary: The NFL announced a major change to the Pro Bowl on Wednesday, bringing an end to the league’s annual all star game while keeping the Pro Bowl designation fo...
articles.body:
The NFL announced a major change to the Pro Bowl on Wednesday, bringing an end to the league's annual all star game while keeping the Pro Bowl designation for the players who earn it. Beginning with the 2026 season, the league will no longer stage an AFC vs. NFC Pro Bowl game or the Pro Bowl Games format that had replaced the traditional contest.

Instead, the NFL plans to make being selected to the Pro Bowl a more meaningful individual honor. A total of 88 players will be selected each season, with no replacement selections. The players will continue to be chosen through an equal weighted voting process involving fans, players and coaches.

The league's decision comes after several years of changes to the Pro Bowl failed to generate the level of interest the NFL wanted. The traditional tackle football game was replaced by flag football in 2023, along with a variety of skills competitions. Despite those changes, the event continued to face questions about player participation, competitiveness and overall importance.

NFL officials said the new approach is designed to put the focus back on what the Pro Bowl is supposed to represent: recognizing the best players in the league. Rather than asking selected players to participate in an exhibition game, the NFL will emphasize the achievement itself and create a larger celebration around the players who receive the honor.

The Pro Bowl class will be announced in late December through an expanded presentation across NFL platforms, team channels, social media and broadcast partners. The league also plans to provide players with lasting recognition, including a Pro Bowl designation on their uniforms and a personalized commemorative trading card.

The change marks the end of one of the NFL's longest running traditions. While fans will no longer get to watch the league's stars compete in a Pro Bowl game, the Pro Bowl name will remain part of a player's resume. The NFL is betting that making the honor more exclusive and focused on regular-season performance will restore some of the prestige the event has lost over the years.

articles.title: NFL announces end of the Pro Bowl − but it was already dead
articles.summary: The NFL will officially eliminate the Pro Bowl as a competition. Here's what they'll do instead.
articles.body:
Apparently a Pro Bowl, well, event that included Joe Flacco and Shedeur Sanders was a bridge too far.

The NFL will officially eliminate the Pro Bowl as a competition and simply apply the honorific to deserving players, many of whom have contract escalators for being named a Pro Bowler. The league made the announcement Wednesday, Aug. 26. The move also aligns with the NFL's ongoing initiatives to emphasize player safety. Playing an all-star exhibition, in any form, didn't square nicely with that objective.

Moving forward, the AFC and NFC rosters will continue to be constructed with 44 players apiece. However with no need for last-minute replacements, there won't be a dilution to the honor that had become so commonplace in recent years. Players, coaches and fans will continue to annually supply equally weighted votes to determine the 88 Pro Bowlers.

"The Pro Bowl has always been about recognizing the players who distinguish themselves as the very best in the NFL," said Peter O'Reilly, the NFL's EVP of club business, international and league events.

"A Pro Bowl selection will return to its original purpose, honoring the best of the best. We want that distinction to carry even greater meaning for the players, their families, their clubs and our fans."

That will apparently include a currently undefined way of recognizing a player's Pro Bowl achievement on his uniform.

Pro Bowl format has changed significantly through years

A pure Pro Bowl had not been played since 2021. The league tried an eSports format during the COVID-19 pandemic following the 2020 campaign and had shifted to a "Pro Bowl Games" alternative in recent years that was significantly less likely to cause players serious injuries.

Still, the NFL's biggest stars routinely accepted Pro Bowl status yet avoided any kind of actual on-field participation, some begging off with injuries and/or surgeries, others often unavailable due to the Super Bowl or late playoff runs once the Pro Bowl format du jour was moved ahead of Super Sunday on the calendar (in 2010) rather than being played − with a free trip for the family to Hawaii, where the game was almost always staged from 1980 through 2016 − afterward. Playing in Honolulu also afforded an opportunity for younger and older players and their families to mingle in a somewhat more private environment that was harder to replicate when the Pro Bowl was held on the mainland.

"This direction came directly from our continued conversations with players and what they value most about the Pro Bowl," said Troy Vincent , the NFL's EVP of football operations.

"Being selected by your peers, coaches and fans as one of the very best at your position carries tremendous meaning. We heard clearly that the distinction matters, and our focus is on making the recognition that comes with it worthy of what these players accomplished on the field."

Earlier this year in San Francisco , the NFC defeated the AFC 66-52 in a flag game staged at the Moscone Center, a downtown convention space but not a venue intended for football. Flacco, 41, a Super Bowl MVP 13 years ago but now a journeyman backup who'd never previously been a Pro Bowler, and Sanders, a rookie in 2025 who had an uneven − at best − first NFL season wound up playing for the AFC as replacements after a season in which they were Cleveland Browns teammates. Sanders played in eight games for the last-place Browns in 2025 and ended the year with seven touchdown passes and 10 interceptions. Flacco, who was benched in Cleveland so the team could assess Sanders and fellow rookie QB Dillon Gabriel , ended the year with the Cincinnati Bengals and filled in for injured star Joe Burrow , though he also wound up participating in the Pro Bowl despite missing more than half the season. (It was also a good opportunity for Burrow, who's shown aspirations to play flag football for Team USA in the 2028 Olympics, to hone his skills in a format foreign to NFL football.)

None of the AFC quarterbacks initially named to the roster in 2025 ( Josh Allen , Justin Herbert and Drake Maye ) played in the game, though league MVP runner-up Maye was in the process of preparing to start in Super Bowl 60 with the New England Patriots .

articles.title: Here's the latest on Jonathon Cooper's roster status with the Broncos
articles.summary: "I think we’ll find out soon," Broncos coach Sean Payton said when asked about Jonathon Cooper's status with the NFL.
articles.body:
Jonathon Cooper has an arraignment date for his felony assault case scheduled for Aug. 31 , which is one day after the Denver Broncos are set to finalize their initial 53-man roster for the 2026 season.

After that arraignment, if Cooper's case goes to trial, it could be months away from a resolution. Cooper could face a potential suspension from the NFL, but the league likely won't make a decision on a potential suspension until after the legal process has been completed.

In the meantime, the NFL could place Cooper on the commissioner's exempt list, but the Broncos have not yet heard a decision from the league.

"I don't know," Payton said on Wednesday when asked if he expects to have clarity from the NFL on Cooper's status before the roster deadline. "In other words, I don't know, and you always want clarity, but I think we'll find out soon and you'll find out probably right when I do."

If the NFL places Cooper on the commissioner's exempt list, he could not practice or play in games, but the pass rusher would still be paid and he would be allowed at the team's facility for meetings, conditioning and weight training. Cooper would not count against the 53-man roster if on the exempt list.

"We continue to monitor all legal developments in the matter, which remains under review of the personal conduct policy,'' NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy said in a statement to 9News.

Cooper, 28, is facing five total charges related to two alleged incidents involving his former girlfriend: (1) second-degree assault: strangulation (felony); (2) third-degree assault: knowingly or recklessly causing injury; (3) criminal mischief; (4) violating a protective order; and (5) harassment (repeated phone calls).

Cooper practiced with the Broncos for all of training camp and he played in the first two preseason games. If Cooper is eventually suspended or placed on the exempt list, Denver's remaining top outside linebackers would be Nik Bonitto , Jonah Elliss , Que Robinson and Dondrea Tillman .
